text: An elevator is closed. The workaround uses two more. What if one of those is closed too?
LiftCheck checks the mapped station path. In this labeled replay, closing Assembly's Foley Street elevator reveals a different entrance. Its two elevators are checked as part of the alternative.
Close the second one, and the alternative disappears. Expire the reports, and the answer becomes unknown. No stale green light.
Now switch to current M B T A reports. Pick the entrance and platform you actually use. Results show mapped facilities, source times, and any missing evidence.
Save those choices as a journey. Reload, and they're still there. Up to four station checks share one alert snapshot, instead of mixing evidence collected at different times.
These are real calls to our self-hosted M C P server. The browser and the assistant-facing tools use the same path logic and saved context.
The prototype covers three stations and checks published reports. It does not certify physical access. Alexa device use and rider testing remain unverified.
LiftCheck. Check the path. Recheck the workaround. Source and reproducible tests are linked.
